text:
Marcus Lin: Hey folks — quick review needed on RBAC for SIEM-ready audit export mgmt + confirming we’re audit-logging *all* config changes. We’re about to merge the control plane gates.

Marcus Lin: Current proposal:
- `audit_export.view` (read-only): can view destinations + status/health + filters (but *no secrets*)
- `audit_export.manage` (write): create/update/delete destinations, pause/resume, update filters, rotate creds, send test event
- `audit_export.replay` (sensitive): replay time window to a destination (beta: we may keep this internal-only / support-only)

Marcus Lin: Mapping to roles:
- Console: Workspace Admins + Org Owners get manage. Security Auditor role gets view.
- Private: platform admins get manage; regular workspace admins maybe still manage depending on customer policy.

Marcus Lin: Audit logging: we need explicit audit events for destination create/update/delete + filter changes + enable/disable + credential rotates + replay actions. All must include actor, tenant/workspace, request_id, source_ip/geo (where available), and *redacted* diffs.

Kevin Osei: +1 on splitting replay. I’d prefer we don’t ship replay to customers in beta unless we’re super confident on guardrails.

Kevin Osei: For manage, can we break out “test delivery” as manage? (Seems fine) but make sure it’s logged too. Customers will ask “who sent this test record into Splunk?”

Benji Okafor: From implementation side, easiest if we add two permissions now (`audit_export.view`, `audit_export.manage`) and keep replay behind an internal feature flag + separate permission (`audit_export.replay`).

Benji Okafor: Question: should Security Auditor be able to see destination endpoints (e.g., Splunk URL / S3 bucket name)? That’s sometimes sensitive.

Marcus Lin: Good call. I think yes, endpoints/bucket names are okay for view (auditors need to validate where logs are going), but we should consider masking where possible (e.g., show bucket, hide full prefix path?)

Olga Petrov: From GRC POV: we need at least destination type + high-level location (bucket name / HEC host) visible to auditor role. Otherwise they can’t evidence “logs exported to customer-controlled SIEM.”

Hanae Suzuki: Re secrets: strong recommendation:
- We never return HEC token / Datadog API key / AWS secret access key after create.
- Console should display `credential_last4` (or token “hint”), `created_at`, `rotated_at`.
- Update/rotate endpoint accepts new secret, but GET never returns secret.

Hanae Suzuki: For S3, if we’re supporting access keys at all (vs IAM role), same rule: do not expose. Also make sure audit event payload doesn’t leak them via “diffs.”

Ethan Park: On the policy engine side we can do:
- `GET /audit-export/destinations*` requires view
- `POST/PUT/DELETE` requires manage
- `POST /audit-export/destinations/{id}:test` requires manage
- `POST /audit-export/destinations/{id}:replay` requires replay

Ethan Park: We already have `workspace_admin` and `org_owner` roles; Security Auditor maps to `security_auditor` (read-only). For Private, we can map `platform_admin` => manage.

Chloe Martin: For Console UX, we can hide the entire “Security → Audit Export” nav item unless user has `audit_export.view`.

Chloe Martin: Within the page:
- view-only: can see destinations list + health + filters; buttons disabled with tooltip (“need Admin to edit”)
- manage: can create/edit/pause/delete + test
- replay won’t be in UI for beta unless we decide otherwise.

Kevin Osei: Audit event types — naming suggestion (matches our schema conventions):
- `audit_export.destination.created`
- `audit_export.destination.updated`
- `audit_export.destination.deleted`
- `audit_export.destination.paused`
- `audit_export.destination.resumed`
- `audit_export.filter.updated`
- `audit_export.credential.rotated`
- `audit_export.test_event.sent`
- `audit_export.replay.started`
- `audit_export.replay.completed`
- `audit_export.replay.failed`

Kevin Osei: Each event should include destination_id + destination_type + environment (hosted/dedicated/private) + outcome.

Marcus Lin: +1. Also please log *authorization failures*? At least we should have standard “access denied” audit events for privileged endpoints, but we can keep that out of export beta scope if it’s noisy.

Benji Okafor: For diffs: we can include a `changed_fields` array and only include old/new values for non-sensitive fields:
- ok: `name`, `status`, `filter`, `endpoint_host`, `hec_ack_enabled`, `s3_bucket`, `s3_region`, `kms_key_id`
- NOT ok: `token`, `api_key`, secret material, full headers

Benji Okafor: I’ll implement as: store a sanitized snapshot of config in the audit event (allowlist) + `redacted_fields=["token","api_key",...]`.

Hanae Suzuki: Please also treat “endpoint URL” carefully. If customers put basic auth into URL (😬), we should strip userinfo from URLs during validation + storage.

Ethan Park: Good catch. We can add validation to reject URLs containing userinfo (`https://user:pass@host`).

Olga Petrov: One more: do we export these audit events (export config changes) through the export pipeline as well? Auditors usually want that.

Marcus Lin: Yes, they’re just audit events like any other. No recursion risk since the exporter reads from audit log stream; emitting an event about config change doesn’t trigger additional config changes. Just ensure the config-change event does not contain secrets.

Kevin Osei: Works for me. Also: when a destination is *paused* due to repeated failures, do we log that as system actor? (`actor.type=system` / `actor.name=audit-export-worker`)

Benji Okafor: Yep. We already have internal “system” actor semantics in audit schema; we’ll use that for auto-pause/circuit breaker transitions.

Marcus Lin: Cool. Action items:
- Benji/Ethan: implement `audit_export.view/manage/replay` gates + ensure GET responses omit secrets + URL userinfo validation
- Benji: emit audit events listed above with sanitized diffs
- Chloe: Console gating based on view/manage
- Kevin/Hanae: quick sign-off on redaction allowlist once PR is up

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: if no objections in the next couple hours, I’ll mark Security Eng approval for the RBAC/audit-logging approach.

Kevin Osei: :thumbsup:

Hanae Suzuki: :thumbsup: (please loop me on the URL validation bit)
